Medicare Advantage membership is expected to decline in the high teens percentage range in 2026, reflecting deliberate portfolio actions and geographic exits.
Medicaid operating margin is expected to be approximately negative 1.75% in 2026, with management viewing 2026 as the trough year for Medicaid.

Medicare Advantage operating margin is expected to improve by more than 100 basis points to at least 2% in 2026.

ADP reported Q1 fiscal 2026 revenue growth of 7% and adjusted EPS growth of 7%.
Employer Services new business bookings resulted in a record sales volume for the first quarter, with growth accelerating from Q4 of last year.
Employer Services pays per control growth rounded down to 0% for Q1 and is now forecast to remain approximately flat for the full year, down from the prior 0% to 1% range.
More than 80% of new mid-market clients in the 50 to 150 employee space were sold on the Next Gen version of Workforce Now in Q1.

ADP increased its full year client funds interest revenue forecast by $10 million to a range of $1.30 billion to $1.32 billion, driven by stronger average client funds balance growth now expected at 3% to 4%.
PEO revenue growth of 7% exceeded expectations, with average worksite employee growth of 2% in the quarter.
Employer Services margin decreased 50 basis points in Q1 due to integration and acquisition-related costs from the WorkForce Software acquisition.
PEO margin decreased 140 basis points in Q1, mainly driven by higher selling expenses, timing of state unemployment insurance costs, and zero-margin pass-through revenue growth.
ADP Assist recorded more than 5.5 million client conversations over the last year.
ADP is maintaining its fiscal 2026 guidance for 5% to 6% consolidated revenue growth, 50 to 70 basis points adjusted EBIT margin expansion, and 8% to 10% adjusted EPS growth.
MicroVision reported Q4 2025 revenue of $0.2 million, down from $1.7 million in Q4 2024, and full year 2025 revenue of $1.2 million, down from $4.7 million in 2024.
The company provided 2026 revenue guidance of $10 million to $15 million, based on prior MicroVision outlook and continuing Luminar revenue streams.

Cash used in operations plus CapEx for 2026 is expected to be in the range of $65 million to $70 million, a modest increase over 2025 due primarily to the acquisitions of Scantinel, Luminar, and the addition of the Virginia-based aerial systems team.
At the end of Q4 2025, MicroVision had $74.8 million in cash, cash equivalents, and investment securities, plus $43 million available under the current ATM facility.

Subsequent to year-end, MicroVision issued two new senior secured convertible notes totaling $43 million in aggregate principal, of which $19.5 million will repay the current outstanding note balance and interest, with the remainder available for general operations.
Full year 2025 cash-based operating expenses were $45.5 million, a decline of $14.4 million or 24% compared to full year 2024, driven by reduced purchased services and headcount reductions.

The company recorded $29.4 million of noncash asset impairment and adverse purchase commitment charges in Q4, including $16 million related to MOVIA L inventory and $13.4 million primarily attributed to perception software and MAVIN equipment.

MicroVision anticipates additional asset impairment charges of $8 million to $12 million related to its Redmond office lease and $1 million to $2 million in people-related restructuring charges from consolidating operations into Orlando.
The Luminar acquisition brought approximately 30 new customer relationships to MicroVision, and the company has already shipped IRIS units within the first month since the acquisition.

Automotive revenue at scale is expected toward the end of the decade around 2029-2030 ramp-up, with the MOVIA S industrial launch on track for Q4 2025 and the 2026 revenue guidance weighted mostly toward the industrial segment.
Sangamo raised over $130 million in funding since the start of 2025 through nondilutive license fees, milestone payments, and equity financing.
The rolling submission of a BLA to the U.S. FDA for ST-920 in Fabry disease is in progress, with both the nonclinical and clinical modules already submitted.
The FDA reiterated in October 2025 that positive mean annualized eGFR slope at 52 weeks may serve as the primary basis of approval under an accelerated approval pathway for ST-920.
Sangamo anticipates completing submission of the Fabry BLA as early as summer 2026, subject to its ability to secure adequate additional funding.
Process validation lots for ST-920 manufacturing have been completed with acceptable results, method validation is complete, and the first commercial lot has been manufactured.
In April, Sangamo announced a third neurology capsid (STAC-BBB) license agreement with Eli Lilly for up to 5 central nervous system disease targets.
Most of the prior Fabry partnership counterparties from last year have dropped out, often due to regulatory uncertainty, and Sangamo is now in discussions with multiple new potential partners.
Six clinical sites have been activated in the Phase I/II STAND study evaluating ST-503 for chronic neuropathic pain due to small fiber neuropathy, with sites currently identifying patients.
ST-503 received Fast Track designation from the FDA in December for patients with intractable pain due to small fiber neuropathy.
The company acknowledged it has not yet solved its long-term cash runway, with securing a commercial partner for Fabry disease described as its number one focus.
Excelerate delivered Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $122 million (up ~9% sequentially) and net income of $50 million (up 28% sequentially), with a 99.8% asset reliability rate.

Full year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was revised to $480-$510 million, reflecting the delayed startup of the Iraq LNG import terminal, with committed growth capital now expected at $270-$300 million.

The Iraq integrated import terminal startup has been pushed from Q3 2026 into 2027 due to Middle East conflict-driven logistical constraints, with the 60-month contract beginning only once operations commence (~6 months after construction resumes).

Excelerate signed a 9-month time charter with Jordan's NEPCO to deploy the newbuild FSRU Acadia (delivered in early April) starting mid-2026, expected to generate roughly $20 million of adjusted EBITDA this year.

QatarEnergy issued a Force Majeure notice in March on the supply agreement, which Excelerate passed through back-to-back to Petrobangla in Bangladesh, with expected financial impact of approximately $1 million per month while the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

As of March 31, 2026, total debt including finance leases was $1.3 billion, cash was $540 million, net debt was $714 million, trailing net leverage was 1.5x, and the full $500 million revolver was available.

The Board approved a quarterly dividend of $0.08 per share ($0.32 annualized) payable June 4, 2026, and the company repurchased ~148,000 shares for just over $5 million at a weighted average price of $34.07 in Q1 under its $75 million buyback authorization.

The Express FSRU is expected to enter dry dock at the end of Q3 2026 and then redeploy to Pakistan in Q4 to substitute for the Exquisite, which will then enter its own dry dock; 2026 maintenance CapEx guidance is unchanged at $100-$110 million.

Management signed a letter of intent with Seatrium Shipyard in Singapore for the FSRU conversion, with associated costs not yet included in revised 2026 committed growth capital guidance, and the converted vessel is expected to support earnings growth in 2028.

Management reiterated that ~200 million tons of new LNG supply will come online by end of decade and views current conditions as supply disruption rather than demand destruction, framing Express redeployment in 2027 and the FSRU conversion in 2028 as the sequenced growth path.
Full year 2025 total revenue was $249.3 million, with subscription revenue representing 53% of total revenue, up from 45% in 2024.
Fourth quarter 2025 total revenue was $55.3 million, representing a 22.1% year-over-year decline.
Full year 2025 net loss and adjusted EBITDA losses were each reduced by approximately $100 million compared to the prior year.
Fourth quarter 2025 adjusted EBITDA loss was $10.3 million, a 55% improvement from the $22.8 million loss in Q4 2024.
The company ended 2025 with approximately $182 million in cash and marketable securities and no debt.
Full year 2026 revenue guidance is $195 million to $205 million, with adjusted EBITDA loss expected in the range of $24 million to $18 million.
First quarter 2026 revenue guidance is $48 million to $53 million, with an adjusted EBITDA loss in the range of $7 million to $5 million.
The company expects to achieve positive cash flow from operations in the fourth quarter of 2026.
In 2025, the company executed over 15 payer contract renewals representing the vast majority of existing payer subscription revenue, including a 3-year renewal with Elevance.
The company's current pipeline is the largest in its history, with participation in RFIs/RFPs across all 50 states, though none of the government pipeline revenue has been built into the 2026 plan.
Q3 2025 orders grew 4% year-over-year to 3,636 units, while average absorption pace declined 7% to 3.8 per month.
Home closing gross margin declined 570 basis points year-over-year to 19.1%, driven by increased incentives, inventory impairments, higher lot costs, and reduced fixed cost leverage.
Excluding $14.5 million in combined real estate inventory impairments and terminated land charges, adjusted diluted EPS was $1.55, representing a 42% decline from $2.67 in Q3 2024.
Community count reached a company-record 334 at quarter end, up 20% year-over-year and 7% sequentially, with management expecting double-digit year-over-year growth in 2026.
The company reduced lot acquisitions by approximately 5,800 lots or 70% year-over-year while maintaining near-term community count growth targets.
Cycle times improved to approximately 105 calendar days from 110 days in Q2, contributing to a 211% backlog conversion rate.

The Board approved an additional $500 million in share repurchase authorization, with $664 million now available under the program, and management indicated the current quarterly pace of $55 million is the floor for future buybacks.
Q4 2025 guidance includes home closings of 3,800-4,000 units, gross margin of 19-20%, and diluted EPS of $1.51-$1.70, with management expecting higher incentive usage typical of year-end.
Direct cost per square foot decreased 3% year-over-year, though management cautioned that potential tariffs and immigration policy changes could impact costs in 2026.

Management stated that stabilizing land acquisition and development costs are expected to benefit gross margins in late 2027 and into 2028, with the long-term gross margin target remaining at 22.5-23.5%.

Q1 2026 growth is skewed toward Q3 due to strong global stadium and U.S. amphitheater growth concentrated in summer months, with Q4 also shaping up to be very strong, implying AOI weighting more heavily to the back half versus prior years.
Concert cancellation rates are running slightly below the historical industry norm of 1%-2%, with roughly 100 cancellations expected out of ~15,000 shows on sale in 2026.
Amphitheater show count is tracking ahead of last year with ticket sales up over double digits, and early on-site premium sales data is positive days into the season.

Ticketing segment faces a mid-single-digit headwind this year from structural one-time steps taken to limit broker inventory on Ticketmaster's secondary platform, but management still expects Ticketmaster growth for the full year.
Secondary ticketing, previously a low double-digit percent of fee-bearing GTV, is expected to gradually decline into the single digits over the next several years as primary ticketing wins.
The company completed an initial venue securitization raise of just over EUR 600 million collateralized by venues, creating a PropCo-like financing vehicle to fund continued Venue Nation expansion.

CapEx has scaled from $400 million three years ago to $600 million, then $1 billion in 2025, and is expected to be equal or higher in 2026, with venue openings expected to accelerate into 2027 and 2028.
Maintenance CapEx on the concert side is only a couple of hundred million dollars, with Ticketmaster characterized as an extremely high cash flow conversion business.
Venue Nation fan count is expected to grow double digits in 2026 off the prior 65 million base, with growth split roughly evenly between existing venue performance and added venues.

Premium capacity is being scaled from historically 1%-5% up to as much as 25%-30% in new builds and retrofitted amphitheaters (Indianapolis, Dallas), with Hollywood Palladium's Vinyl Room already driving on-site spending over $100 per fan.

Management expects operating businesses to reach EBITDA positive by the second half of 2026, with a target gross margin of 50%.
Eagle Materials achieved record quarterly revenue of $639 million, up 2% from the prior year.

The company has over $1 billion in dry powder for future investments, including $443.7 million in cash and $593 million available under its credit line.

River Park Post Acute in Arizona increased occupancy from 76.3% to 97.1% year-over-year with EBIT up 376%, demonstrating the company's transitioning portfolio potential.
Net earnings rose to $14.6 million or $0.74 per diluted share compared to $4.7 million or $0.24 per share in the same period last year.
Quarterly shipments increased 9.8% year-over-year, driven by contributions from recent acquisitions and stronger demand across nonresidential construction markets.
Average selling prices for the quarter rose 20.3% year-over-year and 4.7% sequentially from Q3.
Gross profit rose $16.3 million year-over-year to $28.6 million, with gross margin improving by 700 basis points to 16.1%.
Cash flow from operations used $17 million in the quarter compared to providing $16.2 million last year, primarily due to a $37.4 million use of net working capital.

The company ended the quarter with $38.6 million of cash on hand and is debt-free with no borrowings on its $100 million revolving credit facility.
Capital expenditures totaled $8.2 million for fiscal 2025 and are expected to be approximately $20 million for fiscal 2026.
